conversations.title: Pricing huddle
conversations.raw:
Maya Chen (CEO): Cash has been tighter than the model we showed in January, and finance wants fewer surprise renewals. We're locking annual billing as the default for every new Northline contract. Monthly is only an exception if I sign off.

Sam Rivera (COO): That matches what I told the pipeline. Annual up front, net thirty. I'll update the order form tonight.

Maya Chen (CEO): The reason is predictability. We can staff onboarding against a year, not a month-to-month maybe.

decisions.statement: Annual billing is the default for every new contract.
decisions.speaker: Maya Chen
decisions.rationale: Cash is tighter than the January model, and onboarding can be staffed against a year.
decisions.sourceQuote: We're locking annual billing as the default for every new Northline contract. Monthly is only an exception if I sign off.

conversations.title: #product-launch
conversations.raw:
#product-launch

Jordan Hale  9:14
Decision for the April release: warehouse exception alerts ship, and the predictive ETA model waits. We don't have ninety days of lane data, so a model would just dress up guesses.

Priya Shah  9:21
CS can work with alerts. I'll write the yard-change note for the five pilot accounts.

Jordan Hale  9:24
I'll own the release call. A loud alert is better than a confident wrong arrival time.

decisions.statement: Ship warehouse exception alerts in April and defer the predictive ETA model.
decisions.speaker: Jordan Hale
decisions.rationale: Ninety days of lane data is not enough to ship a predictive ETA without dressing up guesses.
decisions.sourceQuote: Decision for the April release: warehouse exception alerts ship, and the predictive ETA model waits.
decisions.shortLabel: exception alerts in the April release

conversations.title: Onboarding review
conversations.raw:
Priya Shah (Head of CS): The first pilots are messy in a way a setup wizard will not fix. For the first ten customers we stay white-glove. No self-serve onboarding until those ten are live.

Maya Chen (CEO): Agreed. I would rather have ten references than a signup page that strands a dispatcher at 6 a.m.

Priya Shah (Head of CS): I'll stay the owner. We learn the failure cases in the yard, then decide whether self-serve is even real.

decisions.statement: The first ten customers get white-glove onboarding.
decisions.speaker: Priya Shah
decisions.rationale: The first pilots fail in ways a setup wizard will not catch.
decisions.sourceQuote: For the first ten customers we stay white-glove. No self-serve onboarding until those ten are live.

conversations.title: #eng-architecture
conversations.raw:
#eng-architecture

Alex Okonkwo  4:02
Calling it for this quarter: Postgres remains the system of record. We are not moving to a warehouse-first architecture.

Jordan Hale  4:11
Does that block the lane-history export the ETA work needs later?

Alex Okonkwo  4:16
No. We can replicate out of Postgres. A warehouse-first cutover in the same quarter as the April alerts release is how we miss both.

decisions.statement: Postgres stays the system of record this quarter.
decisions.speaker: Alex Okonkwo
decisions.rationale: A warehouse-first cutover in the same quarter as the April alerts release would miss both.
decisions.sourceQuote: Postgres remains the system of record. We are not moving to a warehouse-first architecture.
decisions.shortLabel: Postgres as the system of record

conversations.title: GTM sync
conversations.raw:
Sam Rivera (COO): I sat with two design partners who will not sign a year before they see a month of alerts. Let's switch the default to monthly billing so a pilot can start without a yearly commit.

Maya Chen (CEO): That walks back the March 3 call. I don't love it. The pipeline is stalling on the annual form, and Sam owns the cash gap if we do this.

Priya Shah (Head of CS): We're opening self-serve onboarding for every new pilot starting next week. I can't be in ten yards and also take the three new logos on the forecast.

Maya Chen (CEO): Then the record changes. Monthly billing is the new default, and self-serve is the new front door.

decisions.statement: Monthly billing is the default so a pilot can start without a yearly commit.
decisions.speaker: Sam Rivera
decisions.rationale: Two design partners will not sign a year before they see a month of alerts.
decisions.sourceQuote: Let's switch the default to monthly billing so a pilot can start without a yearly commit.

decisions.statement: Self-serve onboarding is the front door for every new pilot.
decisions.speaker: Priya Shah
decisions.rationale: Customer success cannot cover ten yards and also absorb the new logo forecast.
decisions.sourceQuote: We're opening self-serve onboarding for every new pilot starting next week.
